chapters.title: Never Outshine the Master
chapters.keys: Always make the people above you feel comfortably superior. If you show off your talents too much, you stir up their fear and insecurity and it backfires. Make your masters look more brilliant than they are, and you will rise. Reversal: If your master is already falling, you have nothing to fear from outshining him and need not be merciful, but if he is still firm, wait patiently until his power fades.

chapters.title: Never Put Too Much Trust in Friends, Learn How to Use Enemies
chapters.keys: Be wary of friends, because envy makes them quick to betray you and familiarity makes them spoiled and tyrannical. Hire a former enemy instead, because he has more to prove and will be more loyal. You have more to fear from friends than from enemies. If you have no enemies, find a way to make some. Reversal: A friend can be more useful than an enemy for dirty work or as a scapegoat, though sacrificing a friend costs you that friend for good.

chapters.title: Conceal Your Intentions
chapters.keys: Never reveal the purpose behind what you do. People who have no clue what you are after cannot prepare a defense. Lead them down the wrong path and wrap them in enough smoke that they see your aim only when it is too late. Reversal: Once you are known as a deceiver, no smoke screen works, so openly play the honest or repentant rogue and you can keep running your schemes.

chapters.title: Always Say Less Than Necessary
chapters.keys: The more you say, the more common and less in control you seem. Say less, and stay vague and open-ended, and even a banal remark will sound original. Powerful people impress and intimidate by holding back. Every extra word raises the chance of saying something foolish. Reversal: Silence can arouse suspicion, especially in your superiors, and sometimes you do better talking a lot like the court jester, using words to hide a deception and seem harmless.

chapters.title: So Much Depends on Reputation - Guard It with Your Life
chapters.keys: Reputation is the cornerstone of power. With it alone you can intimidate and win, and once it slips you are open to attack from all sides. Make yours unassailable and stop attacks before they happen. Learn to destroy enemies by opening holes in their reputations, then stand aside and let public opinion finish them. Reversal: There is none, because if you neglect your reputation you simply let others decide it for you.

chapters.title: Court Attention at All Costs
chapters.keys: Everything is judged by appearance, and what goes unseen counts for nothing. Never get lost in the crowd. Stand out at all costs and make yourself a magnet for attention by seeming larger, more colorful and more mysterious than the timid masses. Reversal: As you rise you must keep changing your methods, because the same act wears the public out.

chapters.title: Get Others to Do the Work for You, but Always Take the Credit
chapters.keys: Use the wisdom, knowledge and legwork of other people to advance your own cause. It saves you time and energy and gives you an aura of godlike efficiency. Your helpers will be forgotten and you will be remembered. Never do yourself what others can do for you. Reversal: Taking the credit is unwise when your power is not yet secure or when you have a master above you, so know when sharing or giving up the credit serves you, as Kissinger did with Nixon over China.

chapters.title: Make Other People Come to You - Use Bait If Necessary
chapters.keys: When you force the other person to act, you are the one in control. Make your opponent come to you and abandon his own plans in the process. Lure him with the prospect of fabulous gains, then attack. Reversal: Sometimes the opposite works better, and a sudden, aggressive first strike shocks and demoralizes the enemy.

chapters.title: Win Through Your Actions, Never Through Argument
chapters.keys: Any win you get through argument is hollow, because the resentment outlasts the change of opinion. Get people to agree through your actions, without saying a word. Demonstrate, do not explain. Reversal: Argument is useful for distracting people and covering your tracks when you are deceiving them or caught in a lie, and then you should argue with all the conviction you can muster.

chapters.title: Infection: Avoid the Unhappy and Unlucky
chapters.keys: Misery is infectious, and you can die from someone else's. You may think you are helping a drowning man, but you are only bringing on your own disaster. The unfortunate sometimes draw misfortune on themselves, and they will draw it on you too. Associate with the happy and fortunate instead. Reversal: There is none; the law applies universally, and ignoring it is at your peril.

chapters.title: Learn to Keep People Dependent on You
chapters.keys: To stay independent you must always be needed and wanted. The more people rely on you, the more freedom you have. Make them depend on you for their happiness and prosperity. Never teach them enough to do without you. Reversal: Dependence runs both ways, and though you might try to stand alone by cornering everything as a monopolist does, that isolates you, so mutual dependence is the better position.

chapters.title: Use Selective Honesty and Generosity to Disarm Your Victim
chapters.keys: One sincere, honest move will cover dozens of dishonest ones. Open-hearted honesty and generosity bring down the guard of even suspicious people. Once that opens a hole in their armor, you can deceive and manipulate them at will. A well-timed gift, a Trojan horse, does the same job. Reversal: If you have a history of deceit, sudden honesty or kindness only looks suspicious, so you are better off playing the rogue.

chapters.title: When Asking for Help, Appeal to People's Self-Interest, Never to Their Mercy or Gratitude
chapters.keys: When you need help from an ally, do not remind him of your past good deeds, because he will find a way to ignore you. Find something in your request or your alliance that benefits him and emphasize it out of all proportion. He will respond eagerly when he sees something in it for himself. Reversal: Some powerful people find an appeal to self-interest ugly and want a public chance to show their charity and feel superior, so learn which kind you face and give those people that chance.

chapters.title: Pose as a Friend, Work as a Spy
chapters.keys: You must know about your rivals, so use spies to stay a step ahead. Better still, be the spy yourself. In polite social encounters, probe with indirect questions so people reveal their weaknesses and intentions. Every occasion is a chance for artful spying. Reversal: Others will spy on you too, so plant false information and surround your truth with lies to control the game.

chapters.title: Crush Your Enemy Totally
chapters.keys: A feared enemy must be crushed completely. Leave one ember burning and the fire will break out again. Stopping halfway loses more than total annihilation, because the enemy recovers and seeks revenge. Crush him in body and in spirit. Reversal: Sometimes it is better to leave a cornered enemy a way out or let him destroy himself, once you are sure he cannot recover, and though crushing someone can breed a long grudge, it is almost always wiser to crush him and do it again if he returns.

chapters.title: Use Absence to Increase Respect and Honor
chapters.keys: The more you are seen and heard, the more common you appear. Once you are established in a group, withdraw for a time and you will be more talked about and more admired. Learn when to leave. Create value through scarcity. Reversal: This works only after you have reached a certain level of power through strong presence, because if you leave too early you are simply forgotten, so at the start make yourself seen everywhere.

chapters.title: Keep Others in Suspended Terror: Cultivate an Air of Unpredictability
chapters.keys: People are creatures of habit who need to see familiar patterns in others, and your predictability gives them a sense of control. Turn that around and be deliberately unpredictable. Behavior with no apparent consistency keeps them off balance and wears them out trying to explain it. Taken to the extreme, it intimidates and terrorizes. Reversal: A familiar routine can lull people and serve as a cover for deception or set up a shocking break from the pattern, and too much unpredictability backfires, especially for a subordinate, by looking like indecision or instability.

chapters.title: Do Not Build Fortresses to Protect Yourself - Isolation Is Dangerous
chapters.keys: A fortress seems the safest answer to a dangerous world, but isolation exposes you to more danger than it stops. It cuts you off from valuable information and makes you a conspicuous, easy target. Circulate among people and find allies. The crowd shields you from your enemies. Reversal: Isolation is almost never right, and its one use is short, small doses for clear thinking, keeping your way back into society open, because it breeds strange ideas and is hard to escape.

chapters.title: Know Who You're Dealing With - Do Not Offend the Wrong Person
chapters.keys: People differ, so never assume everyone will react to your moves the same way. Deceive or outmaneuver the wrong person and he may spend his life seeking revenge. Some are wolves dressed as lambs. Choose your victims and opponents carefully, and never offend or deceive the wrong one. Reversal: There is none; ignorance about people gains you nothing, so learn to tell lions from lambs.

chapters.title: Do Not Commit to Anyone
chapters.keys: Only a fool rushes to take sides. Commit to no side or cause but yourself. Keep your independence and you become master of others, playing them against one another and making them pursue you. Reversal: Push this too far and people will see through you and gang up on you or lose interest, so at times commit to one side, at least for appearance, while keeping your inner independence.

chapters.title: Play a Sucker to Catch a Sucker - Seem Dumber Than Your Mark
chapters.keys: No one likes feeling stupider than the next person. Make your victims feel smart, and smarter than you. Once they believe that, they will never suspect your motives. Reversal: Early in your climb you may need to show your bosses subtly that you are sharper than the competition, and a show of intelligence can sometimes cover a deception.

chapters.title: Use the Surrender Tactic: Transform Weakness into Power
chapters.keys: When you are the weaker side, never fight for honor's sake. Surrender instead. It gives you time to recover, to torment and irritate your conqueror, and to wait for his power to fade. Surrender first and deny him the satisfaction of beating you, because turning the other cheek infuriates and unsettles him. Reversal: When the enemy will not be appeased, martyrdom is the opposite choice, but its effect is uncertain and you are not there to enjoy any power it brings, so surrender is usually better.

chapters.title: Concentrate Your Forces
chapters.keys: Conserve your forces and energy by keeping them concentrated at their strongest point. You gain more by mining one rich mine deeper than by flitting between shallow ones. Intensity beats extensity. When you seek a source of power, find the one key patron who will keep feeding you for a long time. Reversal: The weaker side may do better to disperse, guerrilla-style, as Mao did, and tying yourself to one patron is dangerous if that patron falls, so in turbulent times several sources of power are wiser.

chapters.title: Play the Perfect Courtier
chapters.keys: A court runs on power and political skill, so master indirection. Flatter, yield to your superiors, and assert power over others in oblique, graceful ways. Do not show off, keep your flattery sparing, never bring bad news, never act like your master's friend, and never criticize those above you directly. Master these rules and there is no limit to how far you can rise at court. Reversal: You cannot please everyone, and your very success as a courtier will stir up envy and make enemies.

chapters.title: Re-Create Yourself
chapters.keys: Do not accept the role society hands you. Re-create yourself with a new identity that commands attention and never bores the audience. Be the master of your own image rather than letting others define it. Use dramatic devices in your public actions so you seem larger than life. Reversal: There is essentially none, because even seeming natural takes acting, and the only limit is to avoid overacting, which is simply bad theater.

chapters.title: Keep Your Hands Clean
chapters.keys: You must look civil and efficient, with hands never dirtied by mistakes or nasty deeds. Keep that spotless appearance by using others as scapegoats and cat's-paws to hide your involvement. Let someone else do the dirty work and take the blame. Reversal: Scapegoats and cat's-paws must be used with great care, because they are screens, and if one fails, your manipulation is exposed.

chapters.title: Play on People's Need to Believe to Create a Cultlike Following
chapters.keys: People have an overwhelming desire to believe in something. Make yourself the focal point of that desire by offering them a cause or new faith. Keep your words vague but full of promise, and put enthusiasm ahead of clear thinking. Give your followers rituals and ask them to make sacrifices for you. Reversal: If the group sees through you, an angry crowd will tear you apart, so watch for doubt, keep your bags packed, and consider working on people one at a time, because one sucker is easier to escape.

chapters.title: Enter Action with Boldness
chapters.keys: If you are unsure of a course of action, do not attempt it, because your doubts will infect how you carry it out. Timidity is dangerous, so go in boldly. Mistakes made through audacity can be fixed with more audacity. Everyone admires the bold and no one honors the timid. Reversal: Boldness is a tool for the right moment after careful planning, not a way of life, as Lola Montez shows, and timidity is useful only when feigned to lure people in.

chapters.title: Plan All the Way to the End
chapters.keys: The ending is everything. Plan all the way to it, accounting for every consequence, obstacle and twist of fortune that could undo your work or hand the glory to someone else. Do that and circumstances will not overwhelm you, and you will know when to stop. Reversal: Build in alternatives so a rigid plan does not trap you when fortune shifts, but more people lose through vagueness and improvising than through overplanning, so refusing to plan ahead does you no good.

chapters.title: Make Your Accomplishments Seem Effortless
chapters.keys: Your actions must look natural and easy. Hide all the toil, practice and clever tricks behind them. Act as though you could do much more. Showing how hard you work only raises questions, and teaching your tricks lets people use them against you. Reversal: Your secrecy must seem lighthearted, because grim zeal in hiding your methods looks paranoid, and letting people see a little behind the curtain on your own terms can win you admiration.

chapters.title: Control the Options: Get Others to Play with the Cards You Deal
chapters.keys: The best deception gives the other person what looks like a choice. Victims feel in control while acting as your puppets. Offer options that all come out in your favor, or force a choice between two evils that both serve you. Put them on the horns of a dilemma so they are gored whichever way they turn. Reversal: Limiting others' options can limit your own, so sometimes give them some freedom and watch how they use it to gather information you can use against them later.

chapters.title: Play to People's Fantasies
chapters.keys: People avoid the truth because it is ugly, so never appeal to reality unless you are ready for the anger that disenchantment brings. Life is so harsh that anyone who can manufacture romance or fantasy is like an oasis in the desert. Everyone flocks to that person. There is great power in tapping the fantasies of the masses. Reversal: Fantasy carries danger, because the audience half knows it is being fooled and plays along for amusement, so keep it light and do not go too far.

chapters.title: Discover Each Man's Thumbscrew
chapters.keys: Everyone has a weakness, a gap in the castle wall. It is usually an insecurity, an uncontrollable emotion or need, or a small secret pleasure. Find it by watching gestures and unconscious signs. Once you have it, it is a thumbscrew you can turn to your advantage. Reversal: Playing on weaknesses can set off actions you cannot control, because people driven by emotion do not behave as your plans assume.

chapters.title: Be Royal in Your Own Fashion: Act Like a King to Be Treated Like One
chapters.keys: How you carry yourself often determines how you are treated. Act vulgar or common and in the long run people will disrespect you. A king respects himself and inspires the same in others. Act regal and confident of your powers and you will seem destined for a crown. Reversal: Do not take it so far that you humiliate people or tower over the crowd as an easy target, and do not ignore the mood of the times, as Charles I did to his cost when people had turned against authority.

chapters.title: Master the Art of Timing
chapters.keys: Never seem to be in a hurry, because hurrying shows you control neither yourself nor time. Always look patient, as if everything will come to you eventually. Study the moment and the spirit of the times for the trends that will carry you to power. Stand back when the time is not ripe and strike fiercely when it is. Reversal: There is no power in giving up control of time and drifting at its mercy.

chapters.title: Disdain Things You Cannot Have: Ignoring Them Is the Best Revenge
chapters.keys: When you acknowledge a petty problem, you give it existence and credibility. The more attention you pay an enemy, the stronger you make him. A small mistake often gets worse and more visible when you try to fix it, so sometimes leave it alone. If you want something you cannot have, show contempt for it, because the less interest you reveal, the more superior you seem. Reversal: Disdain must be used carefully, because some small troubles grow and fester if ignored, so learn to tell what is potentially disastrous from what is a mere irritant.

chapters.title: Create Compelling Spectacles
chapters.keys: Striking images and grand symbolic gestures create the aura of power, and everyone responds to them. Stage spectacles for those around you, full of arresting visuals and radiant symbols that heighten your presence. Dazzled by appearances, no one will notice what you are really doing. Reversal: Not sure what this chapter gives here, so nothing is stated.

chapters.title: Think as You Like but Behave Like Others
chapters.keys: Make a show of going against the times and people will think you want attention and look down on them. They will find a way to punish you for making them feel inferior. It is far safer to blend in and nurture the common touch. Share your originality only with tolerant friends and those sure to appreciate it. Reversal: Standing out pays only when your position is already secure and established, so your difference marks your distance from others.

chapters.title: Stir Up Waters to Catch Fish
chapters.keys: Anger and emotion work against your strategy, so always stay calm and objective. If you can make your enemies angry while you stay calm, you gain a decided advantage. Find the chink in their vanity, rattle them, and you hold the strings. Reversal: Be careful and study the enemy first, because some fish are best left at the bottom of the pond.

chapters.title: Despise the Free Lunch
chapters.keys: What is offered free is dangerous, because it usually involves a trick or a hidden obligation. Pay your own way and you stay clear of gratitude, guilt and deceit. It is often wise to pay full price, because there is no cutting corners with excellence. Be lavish with money and keep it circulating, because generosity is a sign of power and a magnet for it. Reversal: Not sure what this chapter gives here, so nothing is stated.

chapters.title: Avoid Stepping into a Great Man's Shoes
chapters.keys: What comes first always looks better and more original than what follows. If you succeed a great man or have a famous parent, you must achieve double what they did to outshine them. Do not get lost in their shadow or stuck in a past you did not make. Change course, disparage the legacy of the overbearing father, and establish your own name. Reversal: A great predecessor's name can sometimes be exploited for its glamour, but that is a trick with limits and does not replace power of your own.

chapters.title: Strike the Shepherd and the Sheep Will Scatter
chapters.keys: Trouble can often be traced to one strong individual: the stirrer, the arrogant underling, the poisoner of goodwill. Give such people room and others will fall under their influence. Do not wait and do not negotiate, because they are beyond redemption. Isolate or banish them, and when you strike the source of the trouble, the sheep will scatter. Reversal: Not sure what this chapter gives here, so nothing is stated.

chapters.title: Work on the Hearts and Minds of Others
chapters.keys: Coercion creates a reaction that eventually works against you. Seduce people into wanting to move in your direction, and a person you have seduced becomes your loyal pawn. Do it by working on their individual psychology and weaknesses. Soften the resistant by playing on what they hold dear and what they fear. Reversal: Not sure what this chapter gives here, so nothing is stated.

chapters.title: Disarm and Infuriate with the Mirror Effect
chapters.keys: A mirror reflects reality, but it is also a perfect tool of deception. Mirror your enemies by doing exactly what they do, and they cannot work out your strategy. It mocks and humiliates them and makes them overreact. Mirror their psyche and you seduce them with the illusion that you share their values, and mirror their actions and you teach them a lesson. Reversal: Pick your situations carefully, because mirroring can have consequences you did not plan for.

chapters.title: Preach the Need for Change, but Never Reform Too Much at Once
chapters.keys: Everyone agrees with change in the abstract, but day to day people are creatures of habit. Too much innovation is traumatic and leads to revolt. If you are new to power or an outsider building a base, make a show of respecting the old ways. If change is needed, make it feel like a gentle improvement on the past. Reversal: If the recent past was painful and bloody, do not associate yourself with it, as Napoleon knew when he set up a sober court unlike that of Louis XVI, so pay attention to the times.

chapters.title: Never Appear Too Perfect
chapters.keys: Appearing better than others is always dangerous, and appearing to have no faults is the most dangerous of all. Envy creates silent enemies. Occasionally display defects and admit to harmless vices to deflect it and seem human and approachable. Only gods and the dead can seem perfect safely. Reversal: Not sure what this chapter gives here, so nothing is stated.

chapters.title: Do Not Go Past the Mark You Aimed For; In Victory, Learn When to Stop
chapters.keys: The moment of victory is often the moment of greatest danger. Arrogance and overconfidence can push you past your goal, and going too far makes more enemies than you defeat. Do not let success go to your head. Set a goal, and when you reach it, stop. Reversal: Not sure what this chapter gives here, so nothing is stated.

chapters.title: Assume Formlessness
chapters.keys: A shape or a visible plan opens you to attack. Give your enemy nothing to grasp, and stay adaptable and on the move. Accept that nothing is certain and no law is fixed. Be as fluid and formless as water, and never bet on stability or lasting order. Reversal: Formlessness is a tool for gaining power, not a go-with-the-flow attitude or resignation to fortune, and using it means seeing events for yourself and throwing out the laws and advice others preach.
